title: Erdős #2 OQ: Exact Maximum Minimum Modulus
description: What is the exact maximum possible minimum modulus M of a covering system? Known: 42 ≤ M ≤ 616,000. The lower bound is from Owens' 2014 construction; the upper bound from Balister et al. 2022. This formalizes the gap problem and proves structural constraints on M.

meta.author: Erdős (1950); Owens (2014); Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, Tiba (2022)
originalContributions: ExactMaxMinModulus: formal definition of the gap problem
exact_max_ge_42: PROVED — M ≥ 42 from Owens construction
exact_max_le_616000: PROVED — M ≤ 616,000 from Balister bound
existence_below_42: PROVED — CS exists with min modulus ≥ m for m ≤ 42
no_covering_above_616000: PROVED — no CS with all moduli > 616,000
moduli_ge_two: PROVED — all moduli ≥ 2 by definition
meta.assumptions: 3 axioms: owens_construction (Owens 2014), balister_upper_bound (Balister et al. 2022), reciprocal_sum_ge_one (density argument)

sections.title: Definitions
sections.summary: Self-contained definitions for congruence classes, covering systems, minimum modulus requirements, and modulus lists.
sections.mathContext: A covering system $\{a_1 \bmod n_1, \ldots, a_k \bmod n_k\}$ covers $\mathbb{Z}$ with distinct moduli $n_i \geq 2$.

sections.title: The Gap Problem
sections.summary: Formalizes **ExactMaxMinModulus**: the largest $M$ such that a CS with min modulus $\geq M$ exists AND every CS has some modulus $\leq M$. States Owens (42) and Balister (616,000) bounds as axioms.
sections.mathContext: $42 \leq M \leq 616{,}000$. The gap is the central open question from Erdős Problem #2.

sections.title: Structural Properties
sections.summary: PROVES: monotonicity of min modulus, all moduli $\geq 2$, $M \geq 42$, $M \leq 616{,}000$, $M \in [42, 616000]$, existence for $m \leq 42$, impossibility above 616,000.
sections.mathContext: Structural constraints: the bounds are tight in the sense that 42 is achievable and 616,001 is not.

overview.problemStatement: What is the exact maximum possible minimum modulus M of a covering system? Currently known: 42 ≤ M ≤ 616,000.
overview.text: Covering systems partition the integers into finitely many arithmetic progressions. The maximum achievable minimum modulus is between 42 (Owens) and 616,000 (Balister et al.).

crossReferences.description: This is an open question from Erdős Problem #2 (Covering Systems)
